**Source access caveat, up front:** every `metaculus.com` URL (FAQ, docs, question pages, public API) returned **HTTP 403** to both WebFetch and curl — Cloudflare bot-blocking. Metaculus findings below come from a Mintlify mirror of their docs, EA Forum/LessWrong crossposts of their own announcements, their Substack, and search-index snippets of the blocked pages. Treat exact UI wording as second-hand where noted.

---

## 1. Metaculus

### Question page anatomy
A Metaculus question is three distinct text fields, not one blob: **Description** (background/context), **Resolution Criteria** (the precise outcome-determining conditions), and **Fine Print** (edge cases and nuances). ([docs mirror](https://mintlify.wiki/Metaculus/metaculus/features/questions.md)) Question types are Binary, Numeric (continuous, linear or log scale), Date, Multiple Choice, and Discrete. Continuous questions are elicited by **entering 25th/50th/75th percentiles**, from which the site generates a smooth CDF (200 discrete points by default), with open or closed bounds. ([question types](https://mintlify.wiki/Metaculus/metaculus/guides/question-types)) Multiple-choice options can be added *after* forecasting has begun, triggering automatic renormalization.

### Community Prediction vs Metaculus Prediction
The **Community Prediction** is a **recency-weighted median**: among *n* forecasts the oldest gets weight 1 and the newest weight *n*, then the weighted median is taken — so roughly half the forecaster base must update to move it materially. The **Metaculus Prediction** was a separate, performance-weighted and *extremized* aggregate; it has been **deprecated since November 2024**. ([aggregation summary](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/) — page 403s, summary via search index; see also [predictgeek overview](https://predictgeek.com/prediction-markets/metaculus/))

### Conditional pairs (the "2×2 arrow" UI)
A conditional pair is a **Parent Question** + **Child Question** producing *two* conditional questions: "If Parent resolves **Yes**, how will Child resolve?" and "If Parent resolves **No**, how will Child resolve?" Metaculus's own announcement describes the display explicitly: *"in the forecasting interface they are in a table, and in the feeds, each possible outcome of the Parent is an arrow, and each conditional probability is a bar."* ([EA Forum announcement](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/qELZknyx8eBg7HskH/metaculus-introduces-new-conditional-pair-forecast-questions), [LessWrong crosspost](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nQhmiKeYPvFaEZfWc/metaculus-introduces-new-conditional-pair-forecast-questions))

Canonical example: Parent = "Bing has 5% market share by March 2024", Child = "Alphabet's market cap below $1T by 2025" → *"In a world where Bing reaches 5% market share, the community predicts Alphabet's decline is 56% likely"* vs 44% in the other branch.

**Auto-resolution logic is the key mechanic:** when the Parent resolves Yes, the "if No" conditional is **Annulled**; when the Child resolves, the surviving conditional inherits that value. Conditionals were admin-created at launch, with community creation planned later. Stated purpose: making implicit models of event-dependency *"explicit so they can be discussed and scored."* There is a dedicated [Conditional Cup tournament](https://www.metaculus.com/tournament/2503/), and conditionals have been used for election-scenario work — e.g. *"dramatically different probabilities for Russian territorial gains in Ukraine depending on which candidate won"* ([State of Metaculus](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/q5ihyrBWiGcRJfd7a/the-state-of-metaculus)). Conditional *continuous* questions were added later ([EA Forum](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/jhNicnLKW6apH6TES/metaculus-introduces-conditional-continuous-questions-to)).

### Question groups
Groups bundle **independent sub-questions** under a shared description/resolution criteria; you are *not* required to forecast every sub-question. They render as **fan graphs** (for date/threshold ladders — "easy to forecast progressively wider distributions the further into the future you predict") or as multiple-choice-style visualizations. Their stated analytical value: grouping mutually exclusive or overlapping binaries *"makes it easier to see which forecasts are in tension with each other."* ([Question Groups: Fan Graphs](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/9861/question-groups-fan-graphs--user-creation/), [Fan Graphs](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/11863/introducing-fan-graphs/), [docs mirror](https://mintlify.wiki/Metaculus/metaculus/features/questions.md)) The API exposes `exclude` vs `unpack_subquestions` handling for groups.

### Resolution norms: Ambiguous / Annulled
Resolutions are `yes` / `no` / numeric, or the two failure states `ambiguous` and `annulled`. Metaculus's stated norm: *"To fully eliminate the potential for a question to be Annulled, the resolution criteria must anticipate all possible outcomes that could occur in the future; there must be clear direction for how the question resolves in every scenario."* An Ambiguous/Annulled outcome *"generally implies that there was some inherent ambiguity in the question, that real-world events subverted one of the assumptions of the question, or that there is not a clear consensus as to what in fact occurred."* Writing guidance stresses tight criteria leaving little discretion, and defining terms with extra care. ([FAQ](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/) / [question checklist](https://www.metaculus.com/help/question-checklist/), both 403 — text via search index)

### Key Factors
Key Factors turn comments into structured research notes: a commenter attaches named drivers of their forecast, and others cast **impact votes** on each. Scoring is concrete: total key-factor impact = mean of |impact votes| (**low = 2, moderate = 3, high = 5**) per factor, summed across the comment's factors. Top-comment ranking blends **upvotes 40% / "change my mind" votes 40% / key-factor votes 20%**; the metric is hidden for comments with no key factors. ([Metaculus FAQ](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/), 403 — via search index)

### AI Benchmark → FutureEval
The AI Benchmarking series has been **rebranded FutureEval**: a **$50k seasonal tournament every four months**, plus a biweekly **$1k MiniBench**, **$175k/yr total**, with hand-picked Pro Forecasters on a question subset as the human benchmark. ([Metaculus Substack](https://metaculus.substack.com/p/metaculus-futureeval-ai-forecasting-benchmark), [FutureEval](https://www.metaculus.com/futureeval/))

Bot-vs-Pro head-to-head scores (`100×ln(bot/pro)`, negative = bots worse):

| Season | Bot team H2H | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|
| Q3 2024 | −11.3 | [−21.8, −0.7] |
| Q4 2024 | −8.9 | [−18.8, 1.0] |
| Q1 2025 | −17.7 | [−28.3, −7.0] |
| Q2 2025 | −20.03 | [−28.63, −11.41] |
| **Spring 2026** | **−1.25** | **[−4.87, 2.37]** |

Q2 2025: 54 bot-makers + 42 in-house Metac bots, 348 questions, 10 Pros on 96; bots worst on multiple-choice (−32.9) vs binary (−14.8) ([EA Forum Q2](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/F2stjK9wHSy3HPEC9/q2-ai-benchmark-results-pros-maintain-clear-lead)). Spring 2026: 173 bots (111 external), 297 scored questions, $50k, 10 Pros on 99 overlapping questions — **first statistically non-significant gap**, though nine of ten Pros still individually outscored every individual bot (top Pro 25.30 avg vs top bot GreeneiBot2 20.49). Metac baseline bots (same prompt, swapped LLM) ranked GPT-5.1-high 11.32 > Claude 4.5 Sonnet High 8.94 > GPT-5.2-high 8.62 > o3 8.46; all 8 high-reasoning variants beat their standard counterparts (p=0.004). Bot-team aggregation peaked around **10 bots**. Survey themes: *"simplicity beats complexity"*, *"research quality is a bottleneck"*, and resolution-criteria edge cases causing *"catastrophic misses."* ([FutureEval Spring results](https://www.greaterwrong.com/posts/wZBbDqzfBjYG58CxK/futureeval-spring-results-pros-beat-bots-but-the-gap-is)) A naive linear extrapolation puts single-prompt baseline bots beating Pros ~**June 2027**.

### "Fermi"/decomposition — **thin**
No shipped Metaculus "Fermi mode" found. Fermi decomposition appears only as *pedagogy* on [Prediction Resources](https://www.metaculus.com/help/prediction-resources/) (decompose into knowable/unknowable parts, Drake-equation example, recommends external Guesstimate). Adjacent real features: experimental **Indexes** (weighted composites of lower-level questions, e.g. an AGI Readiness Index), base-rate tools, and "forecast connection tools inspired by Bayes nets" listed as 2025 explorations ([State of Metaculus](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/q5ihyrBWiGcRJfd7a/the-state-of-metaculus)). Metaculus's [forecasting-tools repo](https://github.com/Metaculus/forecasting-tools) is a bot framework, not a site feature.

## 2. Polymarket & Kalshi

### Polymarket market/event page (verified against a live page)
Polymarket originally ran an **LMSR AMM**, migrating fully to a **hybrid-decentralized CLOB** by late 2022 — orders matched off-chain (no gas to place/cancel), settled on-chain via the Exchange contract on Polygon ([panewslab](https://www.panewslab.com/en/articles/fz20kk02b04n), [docs](https://docs.polymarket.com/concepts/prices-orderbook)).

Structurally: **markets** are single binary Yes/No tradable units; **events** are containers grouping related markets. Multi-market events whose outcomes are mutually exclusive form a **negative-risk group** where *"exactly one market in the group resolves Yes, while every other market resolves No."* Both are addressed by slug ([docs](https://docs.polymarket.com/concepts/markets-events)).

Fetching [polymarket.com/event/which-company-has-best-ai-model-end-of-2026](https://polymarket.com/event/which-company-has-best-ai-model-end-of-2026) shows the actual page stack: title + category tags → **15 outcome rows**, each with logo, name, per-outcome volume, implied %, and *paired* **Buy Yes ¢ / Buy No ¢** buttons (Anthropic 73%, Buy Yes 73¢ / Buy No 28¢) → price chart with **1H / 6H / 1D / 1W / 1M / All** toggles → stats (total volume $1.28M, opened date, end date) → **Rules** with named resolution source (lmarena.ai leaderboard, checked Dec 31 2026 12:00 ET, with explicit tiebreakers) → an **"Experimental AI-generated summary"** context panel → **Comments** (4,312), **Top Holders**, **Positions**, **Activity** (live trade feed), **Related Markets** (cross-links to correlated markets), and an expandable FAQ. Order book with bids/asks/spread sits on the individual market view, with your open orders rendered directly beneath it ([help](https://help.polymarket.com/en/articles/13364444-limit-orders), [orderbook docs](https://docs.polymarket.com/polymarket-learn/trading/using-the-orderbook)).

### Kalshi market page
Kalshi's own Markets 101 collection enumerates the page sections: **Market Rules**, **Rules Summary**, **Additional Details**, **Timeline and Payout**, **Market Outcomes**, **The Orderbook**, **Forecast Graph**, **Price Graph**, **Live Data Graphs**, plus "How are prices determined?", *Suggest a New Market*, *Request Additional Strikes*, *Request to Settle Market* ([Markets 101](https://help.kalshi.com/en/collections/18616614-markets-101)). Identity is hierarchical: **series ticker → event ticker → market ticker** (e.g. `KXHIGHNY`), with the ticker explicitly *not* a substitute for "the title, strike, full rules, source or timeline."

The **orderbook** shows resting order quantity at each price with a **Yes/No dual view** (Yes buy 74¢ / Yes sell 71¢ ↔ No buy 29¢ / No sell 26¢ — i.e. the same book mirrored around 100¢) and a bids/asks toggle ([orderbook](https://help.kalshi.com/en/articles/13823828-the-orderbook)). **Product shape.** An API/SDK forecasting service, not a website of static reports: `pip install` + MCP connectors for Claude.ai, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor; API keys `sk-cho-…`. ## 1. Metaculus

### Question page anatomy
A Metaculus question is three distinct text fields, not one blob: **Description** (background/context), **Resolution Criteria** (the precise outcome-determining conditions), and **Fine Print** (edge cases and nuances). ([docs mirror](https://mintlify.wiki/Metaculus/metaculus/features/questions.md)) Question types are Binary, Numeric (continuous, linear or log scale), Date, Multiple Choice, and Discrete. Continuous questions are elicited by **entering 25th/50th/75th percentiles**, from which the site generates a smooth CDF (200 discrete points by default), with open or closed bounds. ([question types](https://mintlify.wiki/Metaculus/metaculus/guides/question-types)) Multiple-choice options can be added *after* forecasting has begun, triggering automatic renormalization.

### Community Prediction vs Metaculus Prediction
The **Community Prediction** is a **recency-weighted median**: among *n* forecasts the oldest gets weight 1 and the newest weight *n*, then the weighted median is taken — so roughly half the forecaster base must update to move it materially. The **Metaculus Prediction** was a separate, performance-weighted and *extremized* aggregate; it has been **deprecated since November 2024**. ([aggregation summary](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/) — page 403s, summary via search index; see also [predictgeek overview](https://predictgeek.com/prediction-markets/metaculus/))

### Conditional pairs (the "2×2 arrow" UI)
A conditional pair is a **Parent Question** + **Child Question** producing *two* conditional questions: "If Parent resolves **Yes**, how will Child resolve?" and "If Parent resolves **No**, how will Child resolve?" Metaculus's own announcement describes the display explicitly: *"in the forecasting interface they are in a table, and in the feeds, each possible outcome of the Parent is an arrow, and each conditional probability is a bar."* ([EA Forum announcement](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/qELZknyx8eBg7HskH/metaculus-introduces-new-conditional-pair-forecast-questions), [LessWrong crosspost](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nQhmiKeYPvFaEZfWc/metaculus-introduces-new-conditional-pair-forecast-questions))

Canonical example: Parent = "Bing has 5% market share by March 2024", Child = "Alphabet's market cap below $1T by 2025" → *"In a world where Bing reaches 5% market share, the community predicts Alphabet's decline is 56% likely"* vs 44% in the other branch.

**Auto-resolution logic is the key mechanic:** when the Parent resolves Yes, the "if No" conditional is **Annulled**; when the Child resolves, the surviving conditional inherits that value. Conditionals were admin-created at launch, with community creation planned later. Stated purpose: making implicit models of event-dependency *"explicit so they can be discussed and scored."* There is a dedicated [Conditional Cup tournament](https://www.metaculus.com/tournament/2503/), and conditionals have been used for election-scenario work — e.g. *"dramatically different probabilities for Russian territorial gains in Ukraine depending on which candidate won"* ([State of Metaculus](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/q5ihyrBWiGcRJfd7a/the-state-of-metaculus)). Conditional *continuous* questions were added later ([EA Forum](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/jhNicnLKW6apH6TES/metaculus-introduces-conditional-continuous-questions-to)).

### Question groups
Groups bundle **independent sub-questions** under a shared description/resolution criteria; you are *not* required to forecast every sub-question. They render as **fan graphs** (for date/threshold ladders — "easy to forecast progressively wider distributions the further into the future you predict") or as multiple-choice-style visualizations. Their stated analytical value: grouping mutually exclusive or overlapping binaries *"makes it easier to see which forecasts are in tension with each other."* ([Question Groups: Fan Graphs](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/9861/question-groups-fan-graphs--user-creation/), [Fan Graphs](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/11863/introducing-fan-graphs/), [docs mirror](https://mintlify.wiki/Metaculus/metaculus/features/questions.md)) The API exposes `exclude` vs `unpack_subquestions` handling for groups.

### Resolution norms: Ambiguous / Annulled
Resolutions are `yes` / `no` / numeric, or the two failure states `ambiguous` and `annulled`. Metaculus's stated norm: *"To fully eliminate the potential for a question to be Annulled, the resolution criteria must anticipate all possible outcomes that could occur in the future; there must be clear direction for how the question resolves in every scenario."* An Ambiguous/Annulled outcome *"generally implies that there was some inherent ambiguity in the question, that real-world events subverted one of the assumptions of the question, or that there is not a clear consensus as to what in fact occurred."* Writing guidance stresses tight criteria leaving little discretion, and defining terms with extra care. ([FAQ](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/) / [question checklist](https://www.metaculus.com/help/question-checklist/), both 403 — text via search index)

### Key Factors
Key Factors turn comments into structured research notes: a commenter attaches named drivers of their forecast, and others cast **impact votes** on each. Scoring is concrete: total key-factor impact = mean of |impact votes| (**low = 2, moderate = 3, high = 5**) per factor, summed across the comment's factors. Top-comment ranking blends **upvotes 40% / "change my mind" votes 40% / key-factor votes 20%**; the metric is hidden for comments with no key factors. ([Metaculus FAQ](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/), 403 — via search index)

### AI Benchmark → FutureEval
The AI Benchmarking series has been **rebranded FutureEval**: a **$50k seasonal tournament every four months**, plus a biweekly **$1k MiniBench**, **$175k/yr total**, with hand-picked Pro Forecasters on a question subset as the human benchmark. ([Metaculus Substack](https://metaculus.substack.com/p/metaculus-futureeval-ai-forecasting-benchmark), [FutureEval](https://www.metaculus.com/futureeval/))

Bot-vs-Pro head-to-head scores (`100×ln(bot/pro)`, negative = bots worse):

| Season | Bot team H2H | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|
| Q3 2024 | −11.3 | [−21.8, −0.7] |
| Q4 2024 | −8.9 | [−18.8, 1.0] |
| Q1 2025 | −17.7 | [−28.3, −7.0] |
| Q2 2025 | −20.03 | [−28.63, −11.41] |
| **Spring 2026** | **−1.25** | **[−4.87, 2.37]** |

Q2 2025: 54 bot-makers + 42 in-house Metac bots, 348 questions, 10 Pros on 96; bots worst on multiple-choice (−32.9) vs binary (−14.8) ([EA Forum Q2](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/F2stjK9wHSy3HPEC9/q2-ai-benchmark-results-pros-maintain-clear-lead)). Spring 2026: 173 bots (111 external), 297 scored questions, $50k, 10 Pros on 99 overlapping questions — **first statistically non-significant gap**, though nine of ten Pros still individually outscored every individual bot (top Pro 25.30 avg vs top bot GreeneiBot2 20.49). Metac baseline bots (same prompt, swapped LLM) ranked GPT-5.1-high 11.32 > Claude 4.5 Sonnet High 8.94 > GPT-5.2-high 8.62 > o3 8.46; all 8 high-reasoning variants beat their standard counterparts (p=0.004). Bot-team aggregation peaked around **10 bots**. Survey themes: *"simplicity beats complexity"*, *"research quality is a bottleneck"*, and resolution-criteria edge cases causing *"catastrophic misses."* ([FutureEval Spring results](https://www.greaterwrong.com/posts/wZBbDqzfBjYG58CxK/futureeval-spring-results-pros-beat-bots-but-the-gap-is)) A naive linear extrapolation puts single-prompt baseline bots beating Pros ~**June 2027**.

### "Fermi"/decomposition — **thin**
No shipped Metaculus "Fermi mode" found. Fermi decomposition appears only as *pedagogy* on [Prediction Resources](https://www.metaculus.com/help/prediction-resources/) (decompose into knowable/unknowable parts, Drake-equation example, recommends external Guesstimate). Its innovation is **RetroSearch**: agents are served a large *frozen* scrape of the web instead of live pages, making runs reproducible; offline agents perform comparably to live ones. The paper auto-evaluates long agent traces for **hallucination, tool use, and forgetting**. ([arXiv 2506.06287](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06287), [drb.futuresearch.ai](https://drb.futuresearch.ai/))
- **Bench To the Future (BTF)** — a **pastcasting** benchmark: already-resolved questions each paired with a **10,000–20,000 URL frozen corpus** captured as of the forecast date, so the agent can research without future leakage. BTF-3 = 1,007 resolved questions (759 binary, 248 numeric); the live board reports 1,754 questions (1,472 binary / 282 numeric), scored by **Brier** (binary) and **Ranked Probability Score** (numeric), CIs by percentile bootstrap (5,000 resamples). ([arXiv 2506.21558](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21558), [evals.futuresearch.ai](https://evals.futuresearch.ai/))

<result># Landscape & Competitive Research — Catalyst causal-chain prototype

## 1. Catalyst: who they are, what impresses them

The coastalhq page is a client-side SPA; I pulled the underlying record from its public `get_public_scoop` API. Verbatim highlights:

- **Founders:** Justin Zheng ([LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/zhengjustin/)) and Dylan Iskandar ([LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dylaniskandar/), [dylaniskandar.com](https://dylaniskandar.com/)). Iskandar is Stanford math/CS — prior work at **Jane Street**, Amazon NLP, AFRL, and InfinityVM (crypto coprocessors); hobbies listed as trading, poker, piano. Palo Alto, founded 2025, **4–5 people, all engineers**.
- **Funding:** "$20M seed round led by Sequoia and Jump Trading," "90+ angels from a16z, Lux, Thrive, Ribbit, Hyperliquid, Binance, Bybit, OpenAI, and DeepMind networks." Team "from Stanford, DRW, and Citadel." Traction: "**Targeting $1B in daily volume by June**."
- **Thesis (verbatim):** "We believe the future is intent-driven: people should be able to state what they want, and agents should coordinate the execution across the right rails… Catalyst abstracts everything end to end: our agents gather market, social, and alternative data, backtest strategies across historical periods, and execute with clear limits and safety controls."
- **Product:** "Using our **custom query language**, users can backtest strategies across historical periods and deploy them with clear limits and safety controls." Data includes "Twitter and social data, news, on-chain activity, and alternative data like satellite imagery." Site tagline: "Trade at the Speed of Thought" ([catalyst.app](https://catalyst.app/)).
- Flywheel they name explicitly: "Trading provides fast feedback loops through PnL, volume, prompts, edits, and executed strategies, creating **proprietary data that improves the agents over time**."

**Inference — what "good" looks like to them.** This is a tiny team of quant-adjacent engineers (Jane Street / DRW / Citadel / Jump) who already have the execution layer. They do *not* need another chat UI. The assignment is upstream of their stack: turn a vague human belief into something with a **strike, a venue, an entry/exit condition, and a falsifiability test**. They will be impressed by (a) rigor about base rates and calibration, (b) anything that compiles to their existing primitives — a backtestable query, a limit, a stop — and (c) speed/craft in the interaction. They will be unimpressed by a pretty graph that does not terminate in a position.

## 2. FutureSearch — the auditability template

ACX's ["The AI Superforecasters Are Here"](https://www.astralcodexten.com/p/the-ai-superforecasters-are-here) describes a scaffolded frontier model: parallel subagents, 16 sites read, **212 sources cited**, ~$8, minutes not hours. The auditable artifacts were the **"conjunctive chain of requirements"** and four named failure modes. Scott's caveats matter: strong in-distribution, weak on novel long-horizon questions; still a black box on *how evidence was weighted*.

FutureSearch's own [Kalshi case study](https://futuresearch.ai/blog/kalshi-forecaster-case-study) is the most concrete recipe anywhere: scan ~3,500 events → rank by volume → filter to 3–97% price and ≥10 days → **two LLM adverse-selection screens** rejecting insider-info/specialist domains → **six parallel research agents** (current state, historical base rates, key influencing factors, expert opinion, competing YES thesis, competing NO thesis) → **three independent model runs, take the median** → compare to live order book and **rank by disagreement**. ~$0.60/question.

Primitives: `forecast`, `decision`, `multi_agent`, `agent_map`; all question types support conditionals, but their docs note a conditional forecast is **"correlational"** while `decision` targets causal comparison ([docs](https://futuresearch.ai/docs/)). $0.15–$2/question.

Benchmarks worth stealing methodologically: **Bench To the Future** — pastcasting on resolved questions with a frozen 10–20k URL corpus per question to block leakage, scored by Brier/RPS with explicit leakage audits ([arXiv 2506.21558](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21558), [evals.futuresearch.ai](https://evals.futuresearch.ai/)); **Deep Research Bench**'s RetroSearch, which auto-evaluates traces for **hallucination, tool use, and forgetting** ([arXiv 2506.06287](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06287)).

And the killer honesty: their [live track record](https://markets.futuresearch.ai/) shows Kalshi paper +49.8% but **Polymarket −19.6% (−51.7% annualized)**, and their [trader case study](https://futuresearch.ai/blog/kalshi-trader-case-study) admits a **43% average fill rate**, only ~$50k of $100k deployed.

Their failure-mode blog is the best in the field: [agents catastrophize](https://futuresearch.ai/blog/agents-catastrophize) (explain an extreme tail well, then underrate the whole question), [history doesn't repeat](https://futuresearch.ai/blog/history-doesnt-repeat) (base rates extrapolated without checking generating conditions changed), [run agents twice](https://futuresearch.ai/blog/run-agents-twice), and [persist/adapt failures](https://futuresearch.ai/blog/dr-persist-adapt) — agents "lack the metacognitive ability" to notice they're stuck.

## 3. Metaculus — the conditional-pair UI you should copy

*Caveat: metaculus.com 403s to tooling; details are from their EA Forum/Substack crossposts and a docs mirror.*

Three separate fields, not one blob: **Description**, **Resolution Criteria**, **Fine Print** ([docs mirror](https://mintlify.wiki/Metaculus/metaculus/features/questions.md)). Continuous questions are elicited as **25/50/75 percentiles**. Community Prediction is a **recency-weighted median** (oldest weight 1, newest weight n).

**Conditional pairs** are exactly your "multiverse" primitive: one Parent + one Child generate *two* questions — "if Parent Yes, how does Child resolve?" and "if Parent No?" Their announcement describes the UI literally: *"each possible outcome of the Parent is an arrow, and each conditional probability is a bar"* ([EA Forum](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/qELZknyx8eBg7HskH/metaculus-introduces-new-conditional-pair-forecast-questions)). Critically, **when the Parent resolves Yes, the "if No" branch is Annulled** — branches die, they don't linger. Stated purpose: make implicit dependency models *"explicit so they can be discussed and scored."*

**Question groups** render as **fan graphs** and exist so you can see *"which forecasts are in tension with each other."* Resolution norms are strict: *"the resolution criteria must anticipate all possible outcomes… there must be clear direction for how the question resolves in every scenario,"* else Ambiguous/Annulled.

**Key Factors** turn comments into structured drivers with **impact votes** (low=2, moderate=3, high=5), summed per comment.

**FutureEval** (rebranded AI Benchmark, $50k seasonal + $1k MiniBench, $175k/yr): bot-vs-Pro head-to-head went −20.03 (Q2 2025) → **−1.25 [−4.87, 2.37] in Spring 2026** — the first statistically non-significant gap, though 9 of 10 Pros still beat every individual bot ([results](https://www.greaterwrong.com/posts/wZBbDqzfBjYG58CxK/futureeval-spring-results-pros-beat-bots-but-the-gap-is)). Themes: *"simplicity beats complexity,"* research quality is the bottleneck, resolution-criteria edge cases cause *"catastrophic misses,"* and bot-team aggregation peaks around **10 bots**. **No shipped Fermi/decomposition feature exists** — "forecast connection tools inspired by Bayes nets" are listed only as exploration. *Unverified:* "Fermat" as a causal-finance tool and "Cassandra" in this space — no evidence either exists.

## 5. Synthesis

**(a) What users of these tools actually value.** Not the probability — the *decomposition*. Metaculus's Key Factors, FutureSearch's six-agent split, and Bloomberg's SHOK all win because they let a skeptic attack one link rather than the whole number. Second: **operationalization** — Metaculus's obsession with resolution criteria exists because unresolvable questions are worthless, and bot post-mortems name resolution edge cases as the cause of *"catastrophic misses."* Third: **a public, unflattering track record.** FutureSearch showing −19.6% on Polymarket is more persuasive than any benchmark.

**(b) Recognized failure modes of LLM causal chains.**
1. **Narrative bias** — next-token training stitches disparate signals into coherent stories unjustified by evidence; Pax Historia's reviewers found exactly this on long causal chains.
2. **Base-rate neglect / "history doesn't repeat"** — extrapolating frequency without checking whether the generating conditions still hold ([FutureSearch](https://futuresearch.ai/blog/history-doesnt-repeat)); GPT-4 shows base-rate neglect and conjunction fallacy at human-comparable rates ([arXiv 2304.01358](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2304.01358)).
3. **Conjunction fallacy / false precision** — a 5-link chain at 80% each is 33%, but the prose reads as inevitable. Give every chain an explicit conjunctive product.
4. **Catastrophizing** — vivid tail scenarios get over-explained then the aggregate gets underrated.
5. **Observation ≠ intervention** — conditioning on an event is correlational; FutureSearch's own docs flag this, and it's why `decision` exists separately from `forecast`.
6. **Correlated errors across runs** — models inherit the same media priors; ensembling helps but doesn't decorrelate ([arXiv 2605.00844](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.00844)).
7. **Persist/adapt failure** — agents repeat the same search six times instead of pivoting.

**(c) 5–8 ideas that would make the prototype distinctive.**

1. **Compile the chain into a tradeable object.** Terminal state is not a graph — it's a Catalyst-query-language strategy with venue, instrument, entry, stop, take-profit, and sizing. Mirror the negative-risk/multi-leg structure Polymarket and Kalshi Combos already expose. This is the single highest-leverage differentiator.
2. **Conjunctive honesty bar.** Show the product of the chain's link probabilities next to the narrative headline, always. If the story says "obviously" and the math says 18%, surface the gap. This directly inoculates against narrative bias and will read as quant-literate to ex-Jane-Street founders.
3. **Ship the counterfactual as a first-class edit, with annulment.** Copy Metaculus's arrow-and-bar conditional UI and its rule that resolving the parent *annuls* the dead branch. Your "Hormuz opens but Iran is struck" is Metaculus's parent/child pair with a second parent — make the branch collapse visible.
4. **Historical-analog audit panel with an event study.** For every claimed edge A→B, auto-search prior instances and render **CAR with a confidence band** over the event window ([methodology](https://www.eventstudytools.com/introduction-event-study-methodology)). This is the literal answer to "how to audit that," and it is what Kensho's Warren promised and abandoned. Analog-search precedent exists ([ORION](https://app.orionengine.xyz/), [KX temporal similarity](https://kx.com/blog/pattern-matching-with-temporal-similarity-search/)).
5. **Shock propagation, Bloomberg-style.** Let the user perturb one node and have correlated nodes update from a factor model rather than from vibes — and *label* which edges are model-derived vs LLM-asserted. Different colored edges for "historically estimated," "market-implied," and "LLM hypothesis" is a 20-minute build with enormous credibility payoff.
6. **Pastcast self-test.** Run one chain on a resolved 2024–25 event with a date-frozen evidence corpus, BTF-style, and show the Brier score. A prototype that grades itself, and shows a loss, will separate you from every demo they see.
7. **Stop-loss derivation from the graph.** Invert the chain: which single node flipping most damages the thesis? That node *is* the stop-loss trigger, and its market-implied probability *is* your position sizing input. This answers their "what events trigger stop-loss/take-profit" directly and is genuinely novel — nobody in the table above does it.
8. **Adverse-selection screen.** Borrow FutureSearch's rejection filter: flag chains where the counterparty likely has private information, or where the edge is in a specialist domain. Saying "don't trade this" is a strong trust signal.

**(d) Red flags / clichés to avoid.**

1. **A force-directed graph of nouns with no numbers.** Pretty D3 blobs read as a viz exercise. Every node needs a probability, a source, and a market it maps to.
2. **Three-decimal probabilities from an LLM with no calibration story.** "71.3% likely" is the tell. Use ranges (Guesstimate/Metaculus percentiles) or admit the uncertainty class.
3. **Agent-society theater.** "I spawned 50 agents representing OPEC members" is the Aaru/Simile trap — impressive-sounding, unvalidated, and this crowd has DRW/Citadel pattern-matching for it. If you simulate, ground it like Park et al. did and report a self-consistency baseline.
4. **A chat UI with a graph stapled on.** They already ship natural-language → execution. Rebuilding their front door adds nothing.
5. **Backtest with no fill assumptions.** FutureSearch's own 43% fill rate is the cautionary tale; a paper P&L curve that ignores the order book will be the first thing a Jump-backed team attacks.
6. **Treating conditioning as intervention.** Saying "we computed P(oil down | Hormuz opens)" and calling it causal will be marked wrong by anyone who knows Pearl. Name the distinction explicitly — it's a credibility freebie.</result>

You are doing independent internet research for a take-home prototype. Use WebSearch and WebFetch liberally. Do NOT write any files; return a report as your final message.

CONTEXT: The company is Catalyst (https://catalyst.app/), "the agent layer for finance": natural language thesis → live execution across markets (prediction markets, commodities, tokens, private markets). Seed stage, backed by Sequoia, Jump Trading, Lux Capital. Background: https://coastalhq.co/scoop/e3a34548-1964-4b30-96ea-52801a558dd2

THE ASSIGNMENT (verbatim gist): design and build a tool that creates and visualizes causal chains from hypothesized events for a financial use case (e.g. "Strait of Hormuz opens → oil prices decrease — why, and how to audit that"). Users explore a "multiverse" by modifying individual events in the chain and seeing downstream effects (e.g. Hormuz opens but Iran is struck the next day). Wants: black swan risk impact, what events trigger stop-loss/take-profit, whether a hypothesized event actually leads to the desired financial effect. Final stage should help user create a tradeable thesis/strategy. Two use cases: (1) is there a reasonable chain from Event A to Event B? (2) given Event A, what B/C/D can I trade on? Inspiration named in the brief: Metaculus, https://www.astralcodexten.com/p/the-ai-superforecasters-are-here, https://futuresearch.ai/

YOUR JOB — landscape and competitive research:
1. Read the Catalyst coastalhq scoop and catalyst.app. What is their narrative, who are the founders, what would THEY be impressed by in a prototype? Infer what "good" looks like to this team.
2. Read the ACX "AI superforecasters are here" post and futuresearch.ai. Summarize how FutureSearch structures forecasts (their decomposition, evidence, base rates, "agentic research"). What do they show users? What is auditable?
3. Metaculus: how do they present questions, community predictions, conditional pairs ("conditional questions"), question groups, and resolution criteria? Anything on their AI benchmark tournament.
4. Look at adjacent products: Pax Historia (YC, alternative-history agent simulation), Aaru, Simile (agent societies for market research), Polymarket / Kalshi (market UI and how they relate linked markets), Guesstimate / Squiggle / Causal.app (probabilistic modeling UIs), any "scenario analysis" or "causal chain" tools in finance (e.g. Bloomberg scenario, Cassandra, Fermat, any newer 2025-2026 AI forecasting startups). For each: what's the core interaction, what's the truth source, what's delightful, what's the failure mode.
5. Synthesize: (a) what users of forecasting/causal tools actually value, (b) the recognized failure modes of LLM-generated causal chains (hallucinated causality, false precision, narrative bias, ignoring base rates), (c) 5-8 concrete ideas that would make our prototype distinctive and credible to the Catalyst team, (d) 3-5 things that would be a red flag / cliché to them.

Output: a structured markdown report, ≤ 2000 words, with URLs for every claim you got from the web. Be concrete and opinionated; flag uncertainty explicitly where a source was thin or unavailable.

input.description: Research causal modeling approaches
input.prompt:
You are doing independent research + brainstorming on computational modeling for a take-home prototype. Use WebSearch and WebFetch. Do NOT write any files; return a report as your final message. If you discuss the Anthropic SDK / Claude models / structured output specifics, invoke the `claude-api` skill via the Skill tool first rather than answering from memory.

THE PRODUCT: a tool that takes a hypothesized event in natural language (e.g. "The Strait of Hormuz is going to open next week", "Republicans win the House but Democrats take the Senate", "Models more capable than Fable get export restricted by the US", "Photonic chips get adopted faster than expected") and (a) generates an auditable causal chain / graph of downstream events toward financial effects (oil prices, specific tickers, prediction-market contracts), (b) lets the user modify any node ("Hormuz opens BUT Iran is struck the next day") and see downstream effects re-propagate — a "multiverse" of branches, (c) surfaces tail/black-swan risk, stop-loss/take-profit trigger events, and (d) ends with a tradeable thesis. Two modes: verify a chain A→B, or explore A→{B,C,D}.

THE FOUNDER'S BRAINSTORM (raw notes you should take seriously and develop): Markov matrices/steady states; chaotic attractors; iterative refinement à la Newton's method; vertical vs horizontal causality (sustaining dependency like desk-holds-apple vs sequential like dominoes — an earlier cause can be undone without changing the effect, so a particular cause may be unmeasurable); cellular automata / simple rules → heterogeneous outcomes; actuarial/insurance modeling of catastrophic vs incremental outcomes ("getting wiped out"); markets as complex adaptive systems that react to positions taken; LLM agents role-playing entities (like Pax Historia, Aaru, Simile agent societies); compositionality/category theory — increase forecast resolution by refining components (model US election as national average → by state → by county, like a chess engine searching deeper lines); Heaviside/Dirac impulses vs continuous inputs; Kalman filters for isolating signal.

YOUR JOB:
1. Survey the candidate formalisms for representing causal chains WITH intervention/counterfactual semantics: Pearl's structural causal models & do-calculus, Bayesian networks, influence diagrams, scenario/decision trees, Monte Carlo over distributions (Squiggle / Guesstimate style), Markov chains, agent-based simulation, and "LLM-as-simulator". For each: how "modify one node and re-propagate" works, tractability for an LLM-driven prototype, what's auditable, what's fake precision.
2. Survey the LLM forecasting literature briefly: Halawi et al. 2024 "Approaching Human-Level Forecasting with Language Models", FutureSearch's method, Metaculus AI benchmark results, work on LLM causal-graph extraction / causal discovery with LLMs (2024-2026), and calibration techniques (reference classes, base rates, decomposition, ensembling, self-consistency). What actually improves calibration? What is known to be hype?
3. Propose a concrete recommended data model for the prototype (nodes, edges, probabilities, conditionals, evidence, time, "interventions", branches) that is: understandable to a human, composable (a branch is a diff/patch on a graph; interventions compose), auditable (every probability has a rationale + evidence + base-rate), and honest about uncertainty. Show it as a small TypeScript-or-Python-like type sketch plus a worked example on the Hormuz case, including the "Hormuz opens BUT Iran struck next day" intervention.
4. Develop the founder's ideas where they earn their place: which of them map to something implementable in a prototype (e.g. resolution refinement = expand a node into sub-nodes; horizontal vs vertical causality = two edge types; wipe-out = tail-loss/drawdown surfaced separately from expected value; markets-react = reflexivity edges) and which are better left as future work. Be honest about which are decorative.
5. Propose how "final stage → tradeable thesis" could be modeled: mapping terminal nodes to instruments (tickers, prediction-market contracts, commodities), entry/invalidation conditions derived from the chain (the stop-loss = the node that, if flipped, kills the thesis), and how to express it as a compact "thesis card".

Output: structured markdown, ≤ 2500 words, with URLs for literature claims. Opinionated; say what you'd actually build in ~1-2 weeks of solo work versus what's future work.

input.description: Research UI/UX directions
input.prompt:
You are doing independent UI/UX research + design brainstorming for a take-home prototype. Use WebSearch and WebFetch. Do NOT write any files; return a report as your final message.

THE PRODUCT: a web tool where a user types a hypothesized event ("The Strait of Hormuz opens next week"), the system generates an auditable causal chain / graph of downstream events toward financial effects (oil price ↓, airline stocks ↑, specific prediction-market contracts), and the user explores a "multiverse": modify any node ("...BUT Iran is struck the next day") and watch the downstream effects re-propagate as a new branch. Must surface black-swan / tail risk, which events would trigger stop-loss/take-profit, and end in a tradeable "thesis" the user can act on. Two modes: verify a chain A→B, or explore A→{B,C,D}. The brief explicitly says: "engaging for users to explore, easily understandable, actually useful — balance form and function." The builder cares enormously about a beautiful, elegant, delightful UI. It's a solo prototype for the Catalyst (catalyst.app, "agent layer for finance") team to evaluate.

THE FOUNDER'S DESIGN NOTES: visual programming; graph/ontology visualizers of nodes and edges; simulation games / auto-battlers / (maybe) Dwarf Fortress + RimWorld legibility of complex systems; compositionality; "impeccable style".

YOUR JOB:
1. Canvas/graph tech: compare React Flow (@xyflow/react), tldraw, d3 + d3-dag, elkjs / dagre layouts, Sigma.js, custom SVG/Canvas. For a DAG of ~10-60 nodes with branches, which gives the best combination of beauty, control, animation, and dev speed? Note pitfalls (layout jank, edge routing, performance, styling lock-in).
2. Branching / multiverse visualization: survey how people visualize forks and counterfactuals — git graphs, Loom (the tree-of-text tool), timeline forks, Sankey/alluvial diagrams, "ghost" overlay diffs, side-by-side / small-multiples, Observable notebooks, Guesstimate/Squiggle distributions inline in nodes, Metaculus conditional-pair UI, Polymarket/Kalshi market cards. What actually works for "compare branch A vs A′"? What's the cleanest way to show the DIFF between two worlds?
3. Design references for the aesthetic: Linear, Raycast, Vercel, Arc, Family, Perplexity, Kalshi, Polymarket, Bloomberg terminal, Observable, FigJam, Obsidian canvas, Pax Historia, Metaculus, futuresearch.ai, plus game UIs that make complex systems legible (auto-battlers like TFT, RimWorld, Dwarf Fortress, Oxygen Not Included, Factorio). Extract concrete, reusable principles: typography, density, color for probability/uncertainty, motion, progressive disclosure, focus+context, empty states, loading states for LLM generation (streaming graph growth!).
4. Propose 3 distinct design directions with a name, one-paragraph description, what it optimizes, and a rough ASCII wireframe of the main screen for each: e.g. (a) "Instrument" — dense, calm, Linear/Bloomberg-lite; (b) "Sandbox" — simulation-game feel, playful, world-state tiles; (c) "Editorial" — narrative-first, Observable/NYT-graphics, chain reads like an argument. For each, how does the "intervene on a node" interaction feel, and how is the final "thesis card" presented?
5. List 8-12 anti-patterns for graph-based tools (hairball, tiny unreadable labels, uniform node styling, fake-precise percentages, modal hell, everything animated, no keyboard nav, etc.) and the specific remedy for each.
6. Accessibility and theming: dark/light, color-blind-safe encoding of probability and direction (up/down), reduced motion.

Output: structured markdown, ≤ 2500 words, URLs for references. Be opinionated: say which direction YOU would pick for a 1-2 week solo build meant to impress a finance-AI team, and why.

input.prompt:
You are doing independent research on engineering structure for a solo-developer take-home prototype that must be unusually well-structured. Use WebSearch and WebFetch where useful (prefer primary docs). Do NOT write any files; return a report as your final message. If you discuss Anthropic SDK specifics (structured output, tool use, streaming, model ids, prompt caching), invoke the `claude-api` skill via the Skill tool first rather than answering from memory.

THE PRODUCT: a web app; user types a hypothesized event; an LLM-driven engine generates an auditable causal graph of downstream events toward financial effects; user modifies nodes and sees branches re-propagate ("multiverse"); ends in a tradeable thesis. Likely stack candidates: (A) Python backend (FastAPI, uv, pydantic) + React/TypeScript frontend (Vite), or (B) all-TypeScript (Next.js or Vite + Hono/Bun). The repo currently has only a Python .gitignore, so Python is a leaning, not a decision.

THE REPO RULES (from the founder's AGENTS.md): ADRs in ./docs/adr numbered, higher supersedes lower; enduring context as ALL-CAPS root docs (AGENTS.md, ASSIGNMENT.md, PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md); detailed specs/diagrams in ./spec following spec-driven development with INVARIANTS and ANTI-PATTERNS sections; solo dev but wants best practices for commit messages, PRs, and PR STACKS for navigability and legibility. Docker + tests + proper code design + rigorously documented ADRs are "extremely important".

YOUR JOB:
1. Stack recommendation: compare (A) vs (B) for this specific product on: LLM SDK ergonomics & structured output, numerics (Monte Carlo, graph algorithms — networkx vs graphlib), testing ergonomics, Docker simplicity, type sharing between backend and frontend (pydantic → JSON schema → TS types via e.g. openapi-typescript / datamodel-codegen; or shared zod), and dev velocity for one person. Recommend one, with an honest "when I'd pick the other".
2. Repo skeleton: propose a concrete directory tree for the recommended stack (apps/, packages/ or backend/ frontend/, spec/, docs/adr/, tests/, docker/, scripts/, .github/workflows/), with a one-line purpose per directory. Keep it tasteful — no kitchen sink.
3. Docker: a compose setup for dev (hot reload for both sides) and a production-ish build; how to keep it simple for a solo dev; .env handling for the API key; healthchecks.
4. Testing strategy for an LLM app: layers — pure-domain unit tests (graph invariants, propagation, branch/patch algebra) with property-based testing (hypothesis / fast-check); LLM boundary tests using recorded fixtures/cassettes (vcrpy / pytest-recording / msw) so CI runs without API keys; a small eval harness for prompt quality (golden inputs like the 4 example events, assertions on structure like DAG-ness, probability bounds, citations present); frontend component tests (vitest + testing-library) and a smoke e2e (playwright) — and what to SKIP for a prototype.
5. ADRs: recommend a format (MADR 4.x vs Nygard) and a template with sections including Context, Decision, Alternatives, Consequences, plus the founder's requirement that specs carry Invariants and Anti-patterns. Tooling (adr-tools, log4brains, or just markdown). Propose the first 6-8 ADRs this project will need to write (titles + one-line gist each).
6. Spec-driven development: what a good ./spec document looks like for a feature like "branching/interventions" — sections, how invariants are phrased so they map to property tests, how anti-patterns are phrased. Cite sources on spec-driven dev if there are good ones (2025-2026 material on SDD with coding agents welcome).
7. Git hygiene for solo + agents: conventional commits, PR stacks tooling (Graphite vs git-spice vs jj vs git-branchless vs plain gh), a recommended branch naming + stack workflow, minimal GitHub Actions CI (lint, typecheck, test, docker build), pre-commit hooks (ruff, mypy/pyright, biome/eslint+prettier).
8. Data sources worth wiring for grounding (optional): Polymarket Gamma API, Kalshi API, Metaculus API, yfinance, FRED — auth requirements, rate limits, and whether they're worth it in v1.

Output: structured markdown, ≤ 2500 words, URLs for tooling claims. Opinionated and concrete; flag anything you're unsure about.

<result># Causal-Chain Forecasting: Formalism Survey + Recommended Build

*Research report. No files written. All literature claims linked.*

---

## 1. Formalisms for causal chains with intervention semantics

The requirement "modify one node, re-propagate downstream" is exactly Pearl's rung 2 (`do(X=x)`: sever incoming edges, propagate to descendants only). Rung 3 (counterfactuals: "what would have happened") needs a *fully specified* SCM with exogenous noise terms you will not have. Build for rung 2; be honest that rung 3 is out of reach ([Pearl's causal hierarchy](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/pearl-s-causal-hierarchy-pch)).

| Formalism | "Modify a node" | Tractable for LLM prototype? | Auditable | Fake-precision risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Pearl SCM + do-calculus** | Native: `do()` cuts parent edges | Semantics yes, identification math no (no data to identify from) | Very — graph *is* the argument | Low, if you don't claim identification |
| **Discrete Bayes net (full CPTs)** | Set evidence, re-infer | ✗ — 2^k elicitation per node; LLM invents numbers | Table is unreadable at k>3 | **High** |
| **Bayes net w/ noisy-OR / log-odds aggregation** | Recompute child logit | ✓✓ **Best fit** — O(parents) numbers | Each edge = one number + one rationale | Medium, manageable |
| **Influence diagrams** | Add decision + utility nodes | ✓ as a thin layer on the above (terminal payoff nodes) | ✓ | Low |
| **Scenario/decision trees** | Prune/regraft a subtree | ✓ but explodes; no shared downstream nodes | Very readable | Low, but coverage is a lie (branches never sum to reality) |
| **Monte Carlo over distributions (Squiggle/Guesstimate)** | Change a distribution, resample | ✓✓ — this is your *execution engine* ([Squiggle](https://www.squiggle-language.com/), [Squiggle AI](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/7worWgggeHL3Eb7wq/introducing-squiggle-ai)) | ✓ if every distribution has a source | Medium — pretty histograms from invented parameters |
| **Markov chains / steady state** | Change transition matrix | Steady states are the **wrong question** — these events are one-shot and non-ergodic | — | **High** (stationarity is a fiction here) |
| **Dynamic Bayes net (time-unrolled DAG)** | Same as BN, per time slice | ✓ — the *legitimate* form of the founder's Markov idea; also how you legalize feedback loops | ✓ | Low |
| **Agent-based / LLM role-play sim** | Change an agent's beliefs | ✗ for v1 — no validation story, high variance, expensive | ✗ (black box) | **Very high** |
| **"LLM-as-simulator" (freeform narration)** | Re-prompt | ✓ trivially, but nothing is held fixed between branches | ✗ | **Very high** |

**Recommendation: a DAG of resolvable propositions with logistic/noisy-OR edge aggregation, executed by forward Monte Carlo, with `do()` semantics for interventions.** It is a Bayesian network you *sample* rather than solve — which means conditioning ("observe" rather than "intervene") comes free via rejection sampling, and every number stays attached to one edge a human can argue with.

The single most honest feature you can ship: **distinguish `do()` from `observe()` in the UI.** "Hormuz opens" asserted as a hypothesis is `do()` — don't update its parents. "Hormuz opened" as news is `observe()` — it *should* update "a US–Iran deal happened," which changes other downstream nodes. Most competing tools silently conflate these.

## 2. LLM forecasting literature: what actually works

**Halawi et al. 2024, "Approaching Human-Level Forecasting with LMs"** ([arXiv:2402.18563](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18563), [NeurIPS](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/5a5acfd0876c940d81619c1dc60e7748-Paper-Conference.pdf)) — retrieval (LM query expansion → relevance ranking → summarization) + reasoning + ensembling. System Brier-competitive with the crowd on a post-cutoff test set; RMS calibration error .42 vs crowd .38. It *approaches*, not beats. The retrieval pipeline is the load-bearing part.

**AIA Forecaster (Nov 2025)** ([arXiv:2511.07678](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.07678)) — the current recipe: news retrieval → multiple base-model forecasts → **adversarial critique** (generate counterarguments to reduce overconfidence) → **ensembling** → **statistical calibration** (Platt scaling). Reports performance statistically indistinguishable from superforecasters on ForecastBench. Its own finding: *single-run performance is noisier and worse than simple averaging over a few independent generations.* Ensembling is not optional.

**Metaculus AI Benchmark** ([tournament](https://www.metaculus.com/aib/), [Q2 2025 results](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/Surnjh8A4WjgtQTkZ/q2-ai-benchmark-results-pros-maintain-clear-lead)) — Pro forecasters still beat the top-10 bot team at p≈1e-5; bots beat the median member of the public. Recent bots land top ~3–5% of human field in Metaculus Cups ([2026 roundup](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/Spyz3wESZu2eeqhDj/ai-forecasting-in-2026-what-11-analyses-say)). Naive extrapolation puts bots past Pros ~2027. Translation: **your edge is not raw probability accuracy — it's structure, auditability, and instrument mapping.**

**Paleka et al., ICLR 2025, "Consistency Checks for LM Forecasters"** ([arXiv:2412.18544](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.18544)) — LLM forecasters are *logically incoherent* (P(A) and P(¬A) both high; violations of Cond, AndOr, ExpEvidence). Their arbitrage-based consistency metric correlates with ground-truth Brier. **This is free QA for your product**: your graph gives you consistency constraints for nothing, and you can score a chain before any event resolves.

**LLM causal discovery** ([IJCAI 2025 survey](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2025/1186.pdf)) — LLMs are decent at *proposing* edges from domain knowledge, unstable at *asserting* them: run-to-run inconsistency, no grounding/attribution, and results plausibly reflect memorization of documented relationships. There's a 2025 paper literally titled ["LLM Cannot Discover Causality, and Should Be Restricted to Non-Decisional Support in Causal Discovery"](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.00844). Design accordingly: **LLM proposes, human disposes, evidence adjudicates.**

**Known hype:** LLM agent societies as forecasters. [AgentSociety](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08691) and commercial voter-sim products (Aaru Dynamo) are impressive engineering with thin public validation ([survey of the space](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.19364) flags inconsistency and authoritative-sounding hallucination as unresolved). Don't build a simulated society in two weeks.

**Verdict on what improves calibration, ranked by ROI:** (1) retrieval of recent news, (2) ensembling ≥5 independent runs, (3) explicit reference-class/base-rate elicitation before the inside view, (4) adversarial critique pass, (5) post-hoc Platt/isotonic calibration *once you have ≥100 resolved questions* (not on day one — it's fitting noise), (6) decomposition into sub-questions — helps comprehension and auditability more than measured accuracy; treat as UX, not magic.

## 3. Recommended data model

```ts
type Prob = { p: number; lo?: number; hi?: number };   // subjective, with an honest interval
type Shape = "impulse" | "step" | "ramp";              // Dirac vs Heaviside vs gradual

interface EventNode {
  id: string;
  claim: string;                  // a RESOLVABLE proposition, not a vibe
  resolution: { criteria: string; source: string; by: ISODate };
  kind: "hypothesis" | "event" | "market";
  prior: Prob;                                        // marginal, before parents
  baseRate?: { refClass: string; k: number; n: number; sources: Url[] };
  evidence: { claim: string; url: Url; direction: +1|-1; weight: number }[];
  payoff?: PayoffSpec;                                // market nodes only
}

interface CausalEdge {
  from: string; to: string;
  mode: "trigger" | "sustain";    // horizontal (domino) vs vertical (desk holds apple)
  strength: number;               // Δ log-odds on child when parent is TRUE
  lag: Duration; shape: Shape; halfLife?: Duration;   // impulse decay
  rationale: string; sources: Url[];
  confidence: "speculative" | "argued" | "documented";
  reflexive?: boolean;            // market → world feedback; must have lag > 0
}

// child aggregation, O(parents) to elicit, O(parents) to explain:
// logit P(child @ t) = logit(prior) + Σ_active edge.strength · shape(t − t_parent)

type Intervention =
  | { op: "do";      node: string; value: boolean; at?: ISODate }   // cuts in-edges
  | { op: "observe"; node: string; value: boolean }                 // updates parents too
  | { op: "insert";  node: EventNode; edges: CausalEdge[] }         // "...BUT X happens"
  | { op: "retune";  edge: string; strength: number }
  | { op: "refine";  node: string; into: EventNode[];               // resolution refinement
                     reconcile: "must-marginalize-to-parent" };

interface Branch { id: string; parent?: string; label: string;
                   interventions: Intervention[]; }   // a branch IS a diff; compose by concat
```

**Why this shape:** a branch is an ordered patch list, so branches compose, replay, diff, and share the base graph. Every probability is either (a) a prior with a base rate and sources, or (b) derived from edges each carrying one number plus a rationale. There is no place to hide an unsourced number.

### Worked example: Hormuz

```
H  "Strait of Hormuz reopens to unrestricted commercial transit for ≥14 consecutive days"
   resolves: IMO/Lloyd's List transit counts, by 2026-11-01 | prior .35
   baseRate: "closure/disruption episodes ending within 90d", 7/9 historically
   evidence: [Omani mediation reported (+, .3, url), 3 tankers still held (−, .4, url)]

H →(trigger, Δlogit −1.6, lag 2d, impulse, halfLife 30d, "war-risk premium unwinds")→ B  "Brent < $68 for 5 sessions"
H →(sustain, Δlogit −1.1, lag 0, step, "insurers reprice only while lane stays open")→ C  "Lloyd's war-risk premium for Gulf transits < 0.4%"
C →(sustain, Δlogit −0.7, lag 7d, step)→ B
B →(trigger, Δlogit +0.9, lag 1d, impulse)→ M1 "Polymarket 'Brent<$70 on Oct 31' resolves YES"
B →(trigger, Δlogit −0.8, lag 3d, ramp)→ M2 "XLE underperforms SPY by >3% over 20d"
B →(trigger, Δlogit +0.6, lag 14d, ramp, reflexive)→ R  "OPEC+ announces output restraint"   // market reacts back
R →(trigger, Δlogit +1.2, lag 5d, step)→ ¬B                                                  // closes the loop, legal because lag>0
```

**Intervention: "Hormuz opens BUT Iran is struck the next day."**

```ts
branch("hormuz-then-strike", [
  { op: "do", node: "H", value: true, at: "2026-10-01" },
  { op: "insert",
    node: { id:"S", claim:"Confirmed kinetic strike on Iranian territory by US or Israel",
            resolution:{criteria:"≥2 of AP/Reuters/AFP", source:"newswire", by:"2026-10-02"},
            kind:"event", prior:{p:0.06} },
    edges: [
      { from:"S", to:"B", mode:"trigger", strength:+2.4, lag:"0d", shape:"impulse", halfLife:"10d",
        rationale:"strike restores risk premium faster than transit data removes it", confidence:"argued" },
      { from:"S", to:"C", mode:"sustain",  strength:+2.0, lag:"1d", shape:"step",
        rationale:"underwriters reprice on threat, not on transit counts" },
      { from:"S", to:"H", mode:"sustain",  strength:−1.9, lag:"3d", shape:"step",
        rationale:"reopening is sustained by absence of hostilities, not by the opening event" } ]},
  { op:"do", node:"S", value:true, at:"2026-10-02" }
]);
```

The `mode` field does real work here. `S → H` is `sustain`: knocking it out **retracts** H going forward even though `do(H)` fired — the apple falls when the desk is removed. `H → B` is `trigger` with an impulse that already fired and decays — the domino stays fallen; removing H later does *not* un-fall B. This is precisely the founder's "an earlier cause can be undone without changing the effect," and it's ~30 lines of propagation code.

Output: `P(M1)` drops from .61 → .18; `P(M2)` .54 → .09; and a new terminal appears where the *original* thesis is maximally wrong — which is the stop-loss (§5).

## 4. Founder's ideas: build, bend, or bin

| Idea | Verdict | Implementable form |
|---|---|---|
| **Vertical vs horizontal causality** | **Build — best idea in the notes** | `mode: trigger \| sustain`; changes retraction semantics on intervention |
| **Heaviside/Dirac vs continuous** | **Build, cheap** | `shape` + `lag` + `halfLife` on every edge; makes timing errors visible |
| **Actuarial / "getting wiped out"** | **Build** | Report payoff *distribution*: CVaR₅, max drawdown, P(ruin) — **never** an EV headline alone |
| **Resolution refinement (compositionality)** | **Build** | `refine` op: expand node → sub-nodes; enforce that children marginalize back to the parent (this is Paleka's consistency check, internalized) |
| **Iterative refinement (Newton)** | **Build** | Generate → adversarial critique → re-estimate, loop until Δp < ε or consistency violations clear. Literally the AIA Forecaster loop |
| **Markets react to positions (reflexivity)** | **Build, constrained** | `reflexive: true` edges with mandatory `lag > 0`; time-unroll the graph so cycles become a DBN |
| **Markov matrices** | **Bend** | Yes as time-unrolled DBN; **no** as steady-state/stationary distribution — these events are one-shot and non-ergodic |
| **LLM agents role-playing entities** | **Bend — narrow use** | Not as outcome simulators. As *red-team personas* ("Iranian regime", "Lloyd's underwriter", "OPEC desk") that propose **missing nodes and edges** the graph lacks. Hypothesis diversity, not simulation |
| **Category theory** | **Bend** | Keep the content (refinement must reconcile with the coarse estimate); drop the vocabulary — it buys nothing in code |
| **Kalman filters** | **Future work** | Real use: tracking your live node probability against the market price as a noisy measurement. Needs a live feed you won't have in week 1 |
| **Chaotic attractors** | **Decorative** | No estimable dynamical system here. Useful only as narrative framing for "regimes." Cut |
| **Cellular automata** | **Decorative** | No mapping from simple local rules to Brent. Cut |

## 5. Terminal nodes → tradeable thesis

The chain must end in a **market node** whose claim is an instrument, not a story: a ticker + direction + horizon, a Polymarket/Kalshi contract ID, or a commodity level.

**Derive the stop-loss mechanically.** Run one-at-a-time flips (`do(n=¬n)`) across every node; record Δ in terminal payoff. The **invalidation node** is the one with the largest adverse swing *subject to two filters*: (a) it resolves **before** the terminal node, (b) it is **publicly observable** (a newswire, a price, a filing). A sensitive-but-unobservable node is a risk you cannot trade against — surface it separately as "unhedgeable."

**Price it against the crowd.** Pull the live prediction-market price for every market node. Your thesis exists only in the gap between your model's implied probability and the quoted price. This also buys you a free calibration harness — every node you create is a question that later resolves, so you can score yourself on Brier/ECE without building a benchmark.

```ts
interface ThesisCard {
  hypothesis: string; horizon: ISODate;
  legs: { instrument: string; direction: "long"|"short"; size: "core"|"satellite";
          drivenBy: NodeId; modelP: number; marketP: number; edgeBps: number }[];
  entry:       { whenNodesTrue: NodeId[]; priceCondition?: string };
  invalidation:{ node: NodeId; flipsTo: boolean; observableVia: string;
                 expectedBy: ISODate; deltaPnL: number };   // ← the stop-loss
  takeProfit:  { node: NodeId; observableVia: string };
  distribution:{ ev: number; p10: number; p50: number; p90: number;
                 cvar5: number; maxDrawdown: number; pRuin: number };
  tails:       { node: NodeId; p: number; pnl: number; hedge?: string }[];  // black swans, listed not averaged
  caveats:     { unhedgeableSensitivities: NodeId[]; crowding: string;
                 weakestEdges: EdgeId[] };                  // lowest-confidence, highest-|strength|
}
```

The **tails** field is the actuarial idea earning its keep: low-probability, high-magnitude branches get their own row with a suggested hedge, instead of being averaged into an EV that hides them.

**Config that matters:** ELK `elk.algorithm: layered`, `elk.direction: RIGHT`, `elk.layered.nodePlacement.strategy: NETWORK_SIMPLEX`, `elk.edgeRouting: ORTHOGONAL` (or SPLINES for a softer look), `elk.layered.spacing.nodeNodeBetweenLayers: 120`, and `elk.layered.crossingMinimization.semiInteractive: true` so re-layouts after an intervention don't reshuffle the world.

**Pitfalls, with fixes:**
- **Layout jank on incremental/streamed nodes.** ELK is deterministic but not stable — adding one node can reorder a layer. - **Edge label collision.** Put the probability/lag on the edge *midpoint chip*, not a free-floating label; use a custom edge with `getSmoothStepPath` and render the chip in an `EdgeLabelRenderer` portal.

## 2. Branching / multiverse visualization — what actually works

Surveyed patterns and their honest verdicts:

- **Git graph (GitKraken/Tower):** branches as colored swimlanes off a spine. Works because *the spine is canonical* and branches are visually subordinate. **Steal: the lane metaphor + branch color as identity.**
- **[Loom](https://generative.ink/posts/loom-interface-to-the-multiverse/)** (multiversal tree writer, [repo](https://github.com/socketteer/loom)): the canonical "multiverse" UI. Its real lesson is the **two-pane split — a tree navigator on the left, one *read* path on the right.** Trees are for *choosing*; linear reading is for *understanding*. Don't make the graph do both.
- **Sankey/alluvial:** beautiful for flow magnitude, terrible for causality + intervention. Skip as the main view; excellent as a **mini "probability mass flowing to outcomes" strip** at the bottom.
- **Ghost overlay diff:** render branch A′ at full opacity, A at 20% opacity dashed, in the *same* layout coordinates. This is the single cleanest two-world comparison and it is cheap to build. Requires computing a **stable union layout** (lay out A ∪ A′ once, then mask).
- **Side-by-side / small multiples:** honest but halves your pixel budget and forces eye saccades for the diff. Use only for ≥3 branches, as thumbnails.
- **[Metaculus conditional pairs](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/17173/introducing-conditional-continuous-questions/):** parent outcome = an arrow, each conditional probability = a bar. Dead simple, extremely legible. **Steal this exact idiom for edge weights.**
- **Guesstimate/Squiggle:** distributions rendered *inside* the node cell. **Steal: every quantitative node shows a tiny density sparkline, not a number.**
- **Polymarket/Kalshi cards:** title → big % → thin bar → volume/liquidity → two buttons. **Steal the vertical rhythm verbatim for terminal (tradeable) nodes.**
- **[Pax Historia](https://wiki.paxhistoria.co/wiki/Basic_Gameplay)'s rewind:** alter a past turn, get an alternate timeline. Confirms the interaction model: **intervene in place, fork implicitly, keep both.**

**The diff, concretely — a three-layer answer:**
1. **Structural diff on the canvas** (ghost overlay): nodes get a state of `unchanged` (neutral), `shifted` (probability moved — show `62% → 31%` with a directional chevron), `added` (in A′ only — solid, accent ring, slides in), `killed` (in A only — ghosted, strikethrough, desaturated).
2. **A "delta rail"** — a ranked list beside the canvas: *"Brent Δ −$9 · airline basket Δ +4.1% · KXOIL-26 Δ −18¢"*. Sorted by |Δ| × confidence. This is the thing a trader actually reads.
3. **A one-line natural-language diff** at the top: *"Striking Iran doesn't reopen the strait — it inverts the oil leg while leaving the airline leg intact."*

Never animate the diff as a crossfade; **animate it as a transition you can scrub**, with a A ⇄ A′ toggle bound to a single key.

## 3. Aesthetic references → concrete principles

**Typography.** One geometric/neo-grotesque UI face (Inter Display, or Geist) + one tabular-figures mono (Berkeley Mono, JetBrains Mono, Geist Mono) for *every number*. `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` globally, or your deltas will shimmy. Linear's real trick: only 3 type sizes (13/15/22) and 3 weights; hierarchy comes from *color and spacing*, not size.

**Density.** Bloomberg's lesson isn't "cram" — it's *no chrome between you and the data*. Kill card shadows, use 1px hairline borders at 8–10% foreground opacity. Node cards ≈ 280×96px, 12px internal padding, 8px grid.

**Color for probability & direction — keep these two axes orthogonal.** This is the most common failure mode.
- *Probability/confidence* → **luminance + fill saturation** of the node (low-confidence nodes are desaturated, hairline-dashed, slightly translucent). Never red-for-unlikely.
- *Direction of financial effect* → **hue, blue↑ / amber↓** (never red/green — fails deuteranopia and carries loss/gain baggage), **always paired with a glyph** (▲/▼) and a sign.
- *Branch identity* → a small ordered palette (violet, teal, amber, rose) used only on the branch's spine/lane and its chip, never on node semantics.
- *Tail risk / black swan* → a distinct **texture** channel, not a color: a hatched border + a small ⌁ mark. Texture survives every form of color blindness and dark/light inversion.

**Motion.** One rule: motion only communicates *causality and provenance*. Edges draw in the direction of propagation (200ms, `ease-out`, staggered 60ms down the DAG) so the user *sees* the chain reason. Everything else is 120ms opacity. No looping, no idle animation, no bouncing springs on a finance tool.

**Progressive disclosure / focus+context.** The graph shows ~6 fields per node max. Click → a right-side **Inspector** (never a modal) with evidence, sources, the distribution, the prior/posterior, and "what would falsify this." Hover → a *lens*: dim everything not on the hovered node's ancestor/descendant path to 15%. This one interaction does more for legibility than any layout tweak.

**Empty state.** Not an illustration — a **launchpad**: three seeded hypotheses as clickable cards ("Strait of Hormuz reopens", "Fed cuts 50bp in March", "TSMC Arizona fab delayed"), plus the two-mode switch (Verify A→B / Explore A→{…}) visible and pre-explained.

**Loading state = the killer feature.** Do *not* show a spinner then dump a graph. **Stream the graph as it's generated:** skeleton node appears at its layer with a shimmering title → title streams in → edge draws to it → probability chip resolves last with a brief number-roll. The user watches the model think in the shape of the artifact. Budget a day for this; it's the demo moment. Reserve layout space ahead of the stream (lay out a predicted 3-layer skeleton) so nothing reflows violently. Also: **stream the reasoning as edge tooltips**, so the audit trail arrives with the structure, not after.

## 4. Three design directions

### (a) "Instrument" — the calm terminal
Dense, quiet, monochrome-with-two-accents. A dark canvas (not black — `#0B0C0E`) with a hairline dot grid, node cards that look like Linear issues crossed with Kalshi market rows, and a persistent right inspector. Optimizes for **credibility and information density** — it reads as a professional instrument a PM would keep open. ## 5. Anti-patterns → remedies

1. **Hairball** (force layout, crossing edges) → layered DAG, left→right, ELK crossing minimization; hard-cap 7 nodes per layer and collapse the rest into a "+4 more" node.
2. **Tiny unreadable labels** → never scale text with zoom below 11px; switch node rendering to a *summary* LOD (title + chip only) under 0.6 zoom instead of shrinking.
3. **Uniform node styling** → four explicit node *types* with different silhouettes: Event (rect), Mechanism (rounded, dimmer), Market Effect (rect + sparkline), Tradeable (card with ticker + price, hairline accent). Shape carries type, color carries direction.
4. **Fake-precise percentages** ("63.7%") → round to 5% and show a band: `60% ±15`. Better: show the sparkline density and the number in a lighter weight.
5. **Modal hell** → one persistent inspector panel, zero modals. Confirmations become undo-able toasts.
6. **Everything animated** → an animation budget: propagation wave, branch creation, number roll. That's it. Everything else ≤120ms opacity.
7. **No keyboard nav** → `⌘K` command palette, `j/k` traverse siblings, `h/l` traverse layers, `E` edit node, `B` branch, `Space` toggle A⇄A′, `?` shortcuts sheet. Arrow keys must move *along edges*, not in screen space.
8. **Lost viewport after re-layout** → preserve the focused node's screen position across layouts (`fitView` only on first load; afterwards `setCenter` on the focus node).
9. **Unauditable claims** → every edge carries a "why" with ≥1 source and a stated mechanism; an edge with no evidence renders **dashed + labeled "asserted"**. Never let the model's confidence and the *evidence's* strength collapse into one number.
10. **Branch explosion** → cap visible branches at 4, force-name them, and auto-collapse the rest into a "runs" list. A multiverse you can't compare is a mess.
11. **Dead ends** (chains that end in prose, not a trade) → every terminal node must resolve to an instrument, a market contract, or an explicit "not tradeable — here's why."
12. **Tail risk buried** → black swans get a dedicated fixed strip, never a node you have to find. They are the point.
13. **Drag-to-reposition fighting auto-layout** → make nodes non-draggable and say so; offer pan/zoom/focus instead. Half-supported dragging looks broken.
14. **Zoom as the only navigation** → add a minimap *and* a breadcrumb of the current path from root.

## 6. Accessibility & theming

- **Dark and light both, with semantic tokens** (`--surface`, `--hairline`, `--dir-up`, `--dir-down`, `--tail`), not raw hex. Design dark-first (it's the finance idiom) but verify light — a graph that only works dark reads as a demo.
- **Contrast:** hairlines may be low-contrast, but *all text and all glyphs* clear 4.5:1, including node labels at min zoom. Chip text on colored fills gets a computed foreground.
- **Color-blind-safe encoding:** blue/amber for direction (safe across deuter/protan/tritan) **plus** a redundant ▲/▼ glyph and a signed number — the rule is *no information in hue alone, ever*. Probability rides luminance/opacity, which is CVD-invariant. Tail risk rides a hatch texture. Branch identity rides color *and* a name chip, since branch lanes are also spatially separated.
- **Reduced motion:** `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` → the streaming propagation becomes instant per-layer reveals (still ordered, so causality is preserved), the number roll becomes a swap, ghost-diff transitions become a hard cut. Never remove the *ordering*, only the tweening.
- **Screen reader / structure:** the DAG also exists as a nested `<ul>` in the DOM (visually hidden or as a "outline view" toggle) — `role="tree"`, each node labeled `"Brent crude falls 12 percent, 61 percent likely, caused by falling insurance rates"`. React Flow gives focusable nodes; add `aria-describedby` to the inspector. Announce re-propagation with an `aria-live="polite"` summary: *"Branch created. 6 nodes changed, 2 removed."*
- **Text scaling:** node cards clamp height but let text wrap to 3 lines then ellipsize with the full text in the inspector — never truncate mid-word at the layout's convenience.
